objective_for_doctor:
Age: 80
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have lower chest pain, right side of the chest pain, and upper chest pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I have a very bad pain in my chest—mostly the lower chest and right side, also upper chest and right breast area. It started fast and feels heavy, sharp, and “scary,” with a lot of sweating and shortness of breath, plus nausea and pain that can go into my biceps and shoulders and even into my upper back and epigastric area.
[ASK] Does the patient have **chest pain/pressure that is worse with exertion or may radiate to the arm/jaw** (possible cardiac ischemia)?
Yes. The pain is in my chest and it radiates into both arms—my biceps—and also my right shoulder. I’m also very short of breath and sweating a lot with it, and it came on quickly.
[ASK] Are you currently having chest pain/pressure that is new, worsening, or occurring at rest (not just with exertion)?
Yes, it’s new and it feels worse. I’m having the chest pain now, even though it’s not a 0/10—it was about 7 out of 10.
